title.narrative: Output 6.4. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen legislation, polices and measures to ensure equal opportunities and treatment in the world of work for persons with disabilities and other persons in vulnerable situations

description.narrative: In December, 2022, the Government of Mozambique (GoM) operationalized gender-responsive measures to ensure equal opportunities and treatment for Persons living with HIV. The Government implemented the VCT@WORK and HIV self-testing in Maputo, Sofala, Tete and Nampula provinces. HIV self-test kits were made available for workers and their families through a partnership of ILO and ECOSIDA (the Business Coalition of Employers against HIV and AIDS), the Informal Sector Association and PSI (Population Services International). In Mozambique the workplace implementation of HIV self-testing. Workers from both formal and informal workplaces were invited to test, particularly emphasizing young male workers and encouraging male engagement. A total of 35,000 HIV self-test kits were distributed, 60% to workers and 28% to their partners and 12% to workplace surrounding communities. Further, the Government has operationalized the National Condom Strategy through massive community-led communication and social mobilization campaign on condoms' use, GBV and sexual reproductive health services and rights, targeting 100,000 youth in and out of schools / in formal & informal workplaces. This has resulted in massive community-led communication and social mobilization campaign on condoms' use, GBV and sexual reproductive health services and rights, targeting 100,000 youth in and out of schools / in formal & informal workplaces. With the distribution of kits, 11,800 informal youth workers have been reached out with HIV self-testing sessions, 35,000 condoms have been made available in three provinces. HIV self-testing sessions for promotion and distribution of condoms. In 2022 and 2023, 55,000 condoms were made available for workers, informal traders and operators in the informal markets and cross border informal traders. The level of access to HIV services for public servants and their families increased, including testing and treatment and social support. n December 2022, the ILO organized a National Seminar with different stakeholders to address the Response Strategy to HIV and AIDS in the Public Service. The round table gathered HR management, HIV focal points, Permanent Secretaries from 22 ministries and was chaired by the Vice Minister of State Administration and Public Affairs. ILO conducted community radio debates and programmes linked to HIV prevention, condom use and VCT@work initiative through the ongoing self-testing campaign in Maputo, Sofala and Nampula provinces. ILO also linked the civil society with the Business Coalition and workers organizations, a key partner in the implementation of the response to HIV and AIDS in the private sector, mainly in the SMEs and in the informal settings.
